projectTab.title: Procurement
projectTab.subtitle: This project's requests, commitments and cost.
projectTab.mrEmpty: No material requests for this project yet.
projectTab.elsewhereHint: Ordering and receiving run in the shared Procurement workspace — the buyer's cross-project queue, not scoped to one project.
projectTab.inventoryNote: Issuing material to site (consumption → project cost) arrives with Inventory.

common.loadFailed: This page could not be loaded.
common.noResults: Nothing to show for this selection.
common.name: Name
common.permissionDenied: You do not have permission to perform this action.

uom.title: Units of Measure
uom.subtitle: Units used across the material catalogue and every procurement line.
uom.codeHint: Up to 20 characters. Uppercase is conventional.
uom.symbolHint: Up to 10 characters — for example m³ or t.
uom.deactivateBody: New materials can no longer be created against this unit. Materials already using it keep it.
uom.deactivateWarning: This list shows active units only, so {code} will disappear from it and cannot be shown again or reactivated. The server also does not check whether materials are still using it.
uom.activeOnlyNotice: This list shows active units only. The API has no status filter, so deactivated units cannot be displayed.
uom.empty: No units of measure yet. Create one before adding materials.

materialCategory.title: Material Categories
materialCategory.subtitle: The operational hierarchy for the catalogue — for example Steel, then Rebar.
materialCategory.parentHint: Leave empty to create a top-level category.
materialCategory.deactivateBody: Deactivating a parent hides its child categories from this tree as well.

spendCategory.title: Spend Categories
spendCategory.subtitle: The financial hierarchy that drives approval routing, tolerance policy and commitment attribution. This is not the same thing as a material category.
spendCategory.parentHint: Leave empty to create a top-level spend category.
spendCategory.deactivateBody: Deactivating a parent hides its child categories from this tree as well.

supplier.title: Suppliers
supplier.subtitle: The suppliers this organisation buys from. Every purchase order, bill and payment names one.
supplier.taxNumberHint: The registration number that appears on the supplier’s invoices.
supplier.currencyHint: Three-letter ISO code, for example USD. Used as the default on new orders.
supplier.paymentTermsHint: Days from the bill date until payment is due. Leave empty if not agreed.
supplier.codeHint: Up to 50 characters and unique within the organisation. Uppercase is conventional.
supplier.empty: No suppliers yet. Create one before raising a purchase order.
supplier.writeOnceNotice: A supplier cannot be edited or deactivated once created — the API has no update endpoint. Check the details before saving.
supplier.noEditWarning: These details cannot be changed later. The name entered here will appear on every bill and payment for this supplier.
supplier.noneYetBody: A supplier has to exist before this document can name one.

material.title: Materials
material.subtitle: The material catalogue. Every MATERIAL procurement line draws its unit from here.
material.baseUomWarning: Once the material is created, the unit of measure cannot be changed. All purchase orders and goods receipts for this material will use this unit.
material.discontinueBody: This material can no longer be added to new requests or orders.
material.discontinueWarning: This list shows active materials only, so {code} will disappear from it and cannot be shown again.
material.activeOnlyNotice: This list shows active materials only. The API has no status filter, so discontinued materials cannot be displayed.
material.empty: No materials yet. Create a unit of measure and a material category first.
material.pickerHint: The full catalogue is loaded and filtered here — the API has no search parameter.

mr.title: Material Requests
mr.subtitle: Internal requests for materials and services, scoped to a project or to the organisation.
mr.submitBody: The request can no longer be edited once submitted.
mr.approveBody: Approved lines become available for allocation to purchase orders.
mr.cancelBody: A cancelled request cannot be reopened.
mr.terminalNotice: This request is {status} and can no longer be changed.
mr.noCloseAction: Closing this request is not available in this release.
mr.partiallyOrderedNotice: Some lines on this request have been ordered. The request remains open until all lines are fully ordered.
mr.workflowNotStarted: Submit this request to start the approval process.
mr.workflowCompleted: This request completed the configured {total}-step approval workflow.
mr.workflowProgressNote: Shows the configured approval chain and current position.

lineError.materialRequired: Choose a material. Material lines cannot be free text.
lineError.quantityMustBePositive: Enter a quantity greater than zero.

scopeError.projectRequired: Project-scoped requests require a project to be selected.

po.title: Purchase Orders
po.subtitle: Orders placed with suppliers. Approving a revision commits cost to the project.
po.totalUnavailable: Order totals are not shown in this list because line data is only available after opening an order.
po.latestRevisionNotice: The revision shown is the most recent one, which is not necessarily the active one.
po.allocationsEmpty: This line is not linked to any material request.
po.approveCommitmentNotice: Approving this revision writes commitment ledger entries totalling {amount}.
po.approveSupersedeNotice: The current active revision will be superseded and reversing entries written for it.
po.approveSupersedeWarning: The reversal uses the revision's full original value, not its uncommitted balance. If goods have already been received, committed cost for this order may be understated.
po.reasonRequired: A reason is required for a revision.
po.reviseBody: Lines are pre-filled from the current active revision. The new revision starts as a draft.
po.cancelBody: All open revisions will be cancelled.
po.cancelCommitmentWarning: Commitment ledger entries already written for this order will remain. Cancelling does not reverse them.
po.exceptionPendingNotice: A goods receipt against this order is awaiting exception resolution. No action is available on the order until it is dealt with.
po.totalIsPreview: The total is calculated here as a preview. The server recalculates each line amount when the order is saved.

lineError.materialRequired: Choose a material. Material lines cannot be free text.
lineError.quantityMustBePositive: Enter a quantity greater than zero.
lineError.priceMustBePositive: Enter a unit price greater than zero. The API does not accept a zero-priced line.

grn.title: Goods Receipts
grn.subtitle: Deliveries recorded against an active purchase order revision.
grn.selectPoHint: Only open orders with an active revision can be received against.
grn.noReceivablePo: There is no open purchase order with an active revision to receive against.
grn.emptyLinesHint: Lines left at zero are not submitted. Fill in only what was delivered.
grn.allLinesEmpty: Enter a delivered quantity on at least one line.
grn.overReceiptWarning: This delivery takes the cumulative received quantity above the ordered quantity. The receipt may be held for review and, if it is, cannot be posted.
grn.overReceiptToleranceNote: The exact tolerance is set per organisation and is not available here, so this warning is a best estimate.
grn.postBody: Posting moves the accepted value from committed to accrued in the commitment ledger. A posted receipt cannot be changed.
grn.cancelBody: A cancelled receipt cannot be reopened.
grn.postedNotice: This receipt is posted and immutable.
grn.exceptionBody: The delivered quantity exceeded what was ordered by more than the allowed tolerance, so this receipt cannot be posted.
grn.exceptionDeadEnd: This held receipt cannot currently be released. Revising the purchase order does not re-evaluate it, so cancel and re-record the delivery against a revised order.
grn.qualityRejectedUnavailable: A fully rejected line cannot be recorded — the API requires an accepted quantity above zero (P6).

lineError.receivedMustBePositive: Enter a received quantity greater than zero, or leave the line empty.
lineError.acceptedMustBePositive: The accepted quantity must be greater than zero. The API cannot record a fully rejected line (P6).
lineError.splitMustEqualReceived: Accepted plus rejected must equal the received quantity.

bills.title: Supplier Bills
bills.subtitle: Bills received from suppliers. Read-only for now.
bills.createBlockedTitle: A purchase-order bill cannot be created yet
bills.createBlockedBody: A bill never records which purchase-order revision it belongs to, so a PO-linked bill can never be matched and its commitment stays at accrued. This is tracked as issue #33. Bills with no purchase order are unaffected.
bills.readOnlyNotice: These screens are read-only. Creating, approving and posting a bill all require endpoints that are not available yet (issue #26).
bills.createSubtitle: For bills with no purchase order — utilities, rent, services and one-off purchases.
bills.nonPoOnlyNotice: A bill raised here cannot be attached to a purchase order. A bill does not record which purchase-order revision it belongs to, so an attached one could never be matched and its commitment would never convert to actual (issue #33).
bills.noProfilesTitle: No expense posting profile is configured
bills.noProfilesBody: A bill line has to name a posting profile that resolves to an expense or cost-of-sales account. None of the profiles in this organisation does. An administrator has to add one before a bill can be created.
bills.invoiceNumberHint: The supplier's own invoice number, as printed on their document.
bills.vatHint: Required. Enter 0 when the line carries no VAT.
bills.expenseProfileHint: Determines the GL account debited when this bill is posted. Revenue profiles are not offered.

lineError.description: Enter a description for this line.
lineError.net: Enter a net amount of zero or more.
lineError.vat: Enter a VAT amount of zero or more. Enter 0 if there is none.

bills.submitBody: The bill can no longer be edited once submitted.
bills.approveBody: Approving clears the bill for posting. There is no reject action over the API, so this cannot be undone from the UI.
bills.postTitle: Post this bill to the general ledger?
bills.postBody: This writes the journal below. It can only be undone by a reversal.
bills.postUnbalanced: The lines do not sum to the bill total. Posting is blocked — this bill is internally inconsistent and should be raised with the backend engineer.
bills.postAccountProblem: The chart of accounts cannot answer which account is Accounts Payable, so the journal cannot be prepared.
bills.reverseBody: A reversing journal is written with the debits and credits swapped. Neither entry is removed. The reversal is refused if any payment has been allocated against this bill.

blockReason.not-draft: Only a draft bill can be submitted.
blockReason.not-submitted: The bill has to be submitted before it can be approved.
blockReason.not-approved: The bill has to be approved before it can be posted.
blockReason.not-posted: Only a posted bill can be reversed.
blockReason.already-reversed: This bill has already been reversed.
blockReason.unmatched: Three-way matching has to complete before this bill can be posted.

payments.title: Supplier Payments
payments.subtitle: Money paid to suppliers, and how it settles against their bills.
payments.createSubtitle: Records a payment to a supplier and the bank account it was drawn on.
payments.accountingDateHint: The date this lands in the ledger. Defaults to the payment date.
payments.bankAccountHint: Only active accounts that allow payments are listed.
payments.amountError: Enter an amount greater than zero.
payments.advanceOnlyNotice: A payment is raised here as an unallocated advance and settled against bills afterwards. Allocating at creation is accepted by the API but never recorded, which would debit Accounts Payable while the bill stayed outstanding (issue #34).
payments.noBanksTitle: No bank account is available for payments
payments.noBanksBody: A payment has to name an active bank account that allows payments. None is configured. An administrator has to add one before a payment can be raised.
payments.approveBody: Approving clears the payment for posting. There is no reject action over the API, so this cannot be undone from the UI.
payments.postTitle: Post this payment to the general ledger?
payments.postBody: This writes the journal below. It can only be undone by a reversal.
payments.postUnbalanced: The allocated and unallocated amounts do not sum to the payment total. Posting is blocked — this payment is internally inconsistent and should be raised with the backend engineer.
payments.postAccountProblem: The chart of accounts cannot answer which account is Accounts Payable or Supplier Advance, so the journal cannot be prepared.
payments.postBankMissing: The bank account on this payment cannot be resolved to a GL account, so the journal cannot be prepared.
payments.reverseBody: A reversing journal is written with the debits and credits swapped. Neither entry is removed. The reversal is refused if any advance allocation against this payment is still posted.

blockReason.not-draft: Only a draft payment can be approved.
blockReason.not-approved: The payment has to be approved before it can be posted.
blockReason.not-posted: Only a posted payment can be reversed.
blockReason.already-reversed: This payment has already been reversed.
blockReason.has-allocations: Reverse the advance allocations against this payment first.

allocation.title: Apply this advance
allocation.subtitle: Settles a posted bill from the unallocated balance of this payment, writing Dr Accounts Payable / Cr Supplier Advance.
allocation.historyUnavailable: Allocations already applied cannot be listed, and cannot be reversed from here — the API returns no allocation identifier (issue #35). Reversing the whole payment is the only correction available.
allocation.billHint: Only posted bills for this supplier, in this currency, with an outstanding balance are listed.
allocation.amountHint: Up to {unallocated} is unallocated on this payment.

blocked.payment-not-posted: This payment has to be posted before its advance can be applied.
blocked.nothing-unallocated: This payment is fully allocated — there is nothing left to apply.
blocked.no-eligible-bills: No posted bill for this supplier in this currency has an outstanding balance.

amountProblem.empty: Choose a bill and enter an amount.
amountProblem.not-positive: Enter an amount greater than zero.
amountProblem.exceeds-unallocated: That is more than this payment has left unallocated.
amountProblem.exceeds-bill: That is more than the bill still owes. Choose a smaller amount.

matching.title: Bill matching
matching.notRunBody: Run matching to compare this bill against the purchase order and, where the bill has material lines, the goods received.
matching.notRunNoPo: This bill is not linked to a purchase order revision, so there is nothing to match it against.
matching.typeThreeWay: This bill contains material lines, so three-way matching will be applied — purchase order, goods receipt and bill.
matching.typeTwoWay: This bill has no material lines, so two-way matching will be applied — purchase order and bill.
matching.exceptionBanner: Variance exceeds tolerance — posting is blocked.
matching.approveExceptionBody: Approving records that the variance is accepted and releases the bill for posting.
matching.postBlockedTooltip: Matching must pass before posting. Open the Matching tab.
matching.postAdvisoryNotice: This check is advisory. An unmatched bill can still be posted, so verify the match before continuing.

commitments.title: Commitment Ledger
commitments.subtitle: Cost committed, accrued and actual, by project.
commitments.committedHint: Purchase order approved, goods not yet received.
commitments.accruedHint: Goods received and accepted, bill not yet posted.
commitments.actualHint: Supplier bill posted to the general ledger.
commitments.selectProjectHint: The ledger is queried per project — there is no organisation-wide view.
commitments.empty: No commitment entries for this selection.
commitments.accuracyNotice: These figures may overstate committed cost. Cancelling a purchase order does not reverse commitments, and revising one after goods were received can reverse too much.
